title: How earthquake waves travel through the ground
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: What are P waves and S waves?
Which earthquake waves are the most damaging?

figure.name: x-wave
figure.note: P waves push and pull the rock: fastest, arrive first

explain.say: When rock slips in an earthquake, the energy spreads out as seismic waves, like ripples from a stone dropped in a pond.

draw.text: How earthquake waves travel through the ground

explain.say: The fastest are P waves, or primary waves. They squash and stretch the rock in the direction they travel, like a push along a slinky, and can pass through solid, liquid and gas.
Next come S waves, or secondary waves. They shake the rock from side to side as they travel, like flicking a rope, and they cannot pass through liquid.

draw.name: x-wave
draw.note: S waves shake rock sideways: slower, no liquids

explain.say: Last come surface waves, which roll along the ground like waves on the sea. They are the slowest but usually do the most damage to buildings.

draw.name: x-wave
draw.note: Surface waves roll the ground: slowest, most damage

faq.a: P waves, or primary waves, are the fastest earthquake waves. They push and pull the rock in the direction they travel and can move through solids, liquids and gases.
S waves, or secondary waves, shake the rock up and down or side to side as they travel. They are slower than P waves and cannot pass through liquids.

faq.q: Which earthquake waves are the most damaging?
faq.a: Surface waves usually do the most damage. They travel along the ground last and slowest, but they make big rolling and side-to-side movements that shake buildings hardest.

faq.q: How do scientists record earthquake waves?
faq.a: They use seismometers, which measure tiny movements of the ground. The record is called a seismogram, and the gap between the P and S waves tells how far away the quake was.

faq.q: How do earthquake waves tell us about the inside of the Earth?
faq.a: S waves cannot travel through liquid, and they vanish on the far side of the Earth from a big quake. That showed scientists that the Earth's outer core is liquid.
asks: How do we know the outer core is liquid?

facts: P waves travel at roughly 6 kilometres per second in the Earth's crust, faster than S waves.
S waves cannot travel through liquid, which shows the Earth's outer core is liquid.

quiz.say: Which earthquake wave arrives first at a seismometer?
quiz.why: P waves are the fastest seismic waves, so they always arrive first.

wrong.1: S waves are slower, so they arrive second.
wrong.2: Surface waves are the slowest and arrive last.
